captions: Let's break down the LAPL Automotive I-P-O —
a thirty-two crore S-M-E issue from an auto-components maker,
expanding into lighting and electronics.
We'll cover what it does, its financials,
where the money goes,
and what it takes to apply on the S-M-E platform.
This is education, not investment advice.
So what does LAPL Automotive do?
It makes automotive components —
chiefly lighting systems and mirrors for vehicles.
It runs two models.
About seventy-eight percent of its revenue is O-D-M —
designing and manufacturing parts for other brands.
The other twenty-two percent is O-B-M —
selling under its own brands, which can carry better margins.
So it's an auto-ancillary play,
riding India's large vehicle and spare-parts demand,
and slowly building its own brand.
Now the financials — healthy, with improving margins.
Revenue rose about forty-one percent,
from sixty-six crore to ninety-three point three zero crore in FY twenty twenty-six.
And net profit jumped seventy-one point four percent,
from five point zero three crore to eight point six zero crore.
Notice that profit grew faster than sales —
a sign margins are improving, helped by the own-brand mix.
The grey market is pricing a premium of around eighteen percent —
but that's unofficial and moves daily.
Where does your money go?
Like the last one, this is a hundred percent fresh issue —
there's no offer for sale.
Every rupee raised goes into the company.
For a manufacturer that's about to expand capacity,
putting all the money to work in the business —
rather than paying out a promoter —
is exactly the right structure.
What does the fresh money fund?
The bulk — about nineteen and a half crore —
sets up a new manufacturing unit,
expanding the company into lighting,
electricals and electronic components.
That's a capacity and product expansion.
Around four point eight crore repays debt,
cutting interest costs.
And the rest is for general purposes.
So most of the money funds real growth —
the kind of use you want to see.
Should you subscribe?
The strengths —
revenue up forty-one percent and profit up seventy-one,
so margins are improving; it's a hundred percent fresh issue funding a new plant and cutting debt; and it's building higher-margin own brands.
The watch-outs — it's a small S-M-E,
so volatile and thinly traded; auto components are cyclical and can depend on a few customers; and a new plant always carries execution risk.
The takeaway —
solid growth and a productive use of the money,
but a small-cap, cyclical bet with expansion risk.
Weigh that before you decide.
Now — how to apply.
LAPL lists on the B-S-E S-M-E platform,
separate from the mainboard.
The minimum is large: one lot is twelve hundred shares,
and the smallest retail application is two lots —
about two lakh twenty-five thousand six hundred rupees.
As always with S-M-Es, expect volatility and thin trading,
so invest only what you can afford to lock up.
Track the live subscription on the B-S-E S-M-E page,
Chittorgarh, or your broker app —
allotment is by lottery if oversubscribed.
Let's recap LAPL Automotive.
An auto-components maker — lighting and mirrors —
growing well,
with revenue up forty-one percent and profit up seventy-one,
and rising margins from its own brands.
The whole thirty-two crore issue is fresh money,
funding a new plant and cutting debt.
But it's a small, cyclical S-M-E,
and the minimum bid is about two lakh twenty-five thousand rupees.
This video explains the IPO for education only —
it is not investment advice,
not a buy or sell recommendation,
and not a prediction of listing gains.
Grey-market premium is unofficial and changes hourly.
Always read the RHP and check the live subscription before you apply.
Thanks for watching.
